title: #bugs · @sara: Safari users can't stay logged in
snippet: Three reports today, all Safari 17. Magic link works, then they hit /app and bounce back to /login. Repro on my MBP.
full_text:
Sara Kim (Support) — 2026-05-04 09:50 PT — #bugs

Three reports today, all Safari 17. The flow is: user clicks magic link in mail.acme-co.com, lands on app.acme-co.com, then bounces straight back to /login. Repros 100% on my Safari 17 MacBook in private mode and ~80% in regular mode. Chrome and Firefox unaffected.

Filing as P1, three customers complaining including Northwind which is a $200k ARR account.

title: CSV Export v2 — Design Spec
snippet: Cursor-paginated streaming export with format options (csv | ndjson) and column selection. Replaces the in-memory v1 implementation.
full_text:
# CSV Export v2 — Design Spec
Author: Lin Chen
Last updated: 2026-05-05
Status: Final (pending implementation)

## Goals
1. Streaming exports up to 10M rows without memory blow-up.
2. Both CSV and NDJSON output (NDJSON for the data-engineering customer segment).
3. Per-export column selection.

## Non-goals
- Row-level transforms / templating. Customers can post-process.
- Backfill of historical exports.

## Design
Replace the v1 implementation in src/api/export/csv.ts with a streaming handler that:
- Reads in pages of 1000 rows using a tuple cursor of (created_at, id) — single-column created_at cursor would skip rows on bursty timestamps. (Same pattern as the orders endpoint, see src/api/orders/list.ts.)
- Accepts ?format=csv|ndjson on the same endpoint.
- Accepts ?columns=a,b,c (whitelist-checked against the export schema).

## Dependency: rate-limit middleware
The new pagination will issue many small DB reads in sequence. The current src/middleware/rateLimit.ts uses an in-memory windowed counter that loses state on instance restart, which already trips during local testing of v2. **CSV v2 cannot ship externally until the rate-limit refactor lands.**

## Rollout
- Land behind csv_export_v2 feature flag.
- Internal cohorts first; Northwind opt-in once rate-limit fix is in prod.
- Targeted external GA: first half of June 2026.
author: lin.chen

title: Rate-Limit Middleware — RFC (Redis sliding window)
snippet: Replace the in-memory windowed counter with a Redis-backed sliding window so the limiter survives instance restarts.
full_text:
# RFC: Rate-Limit Middleware — Redis Sliding Window
Author: Marco Reyes
Date: 2026-05-08
Status: Approved (Priya, Lin)

## Problem
src/middleware/rateLimit.ts uses an in-process Map keyed by req.ip with a windowed counter. We deploy 2-3 times a day and every deploy resets the limiter, which means burst traffic right after a deploy is unbounded. Internal CSV v2 testing also trips this immediately.

## Decision
Redis-backed sliding window using INCR + EXPIRE on a per-key bucket, with a small Lua script for atomic check-and-set. Same Redis instance we already run for cache; no new infra.

## Rejected alternatives
- Token bucket + Postgres advisory lock: more elegant, but a new pattern for the team and would not ship in a week.
- Cloudflare-only rate limit: covers the edge but not the per-account internal limits we need for CSV v2.

## Risks
- Redis memory headroom is ~60% today (Lin to verify Friday). New keyspace will add maybe 5-8% at peak; if headroom drops below 25% we should bump instance size before launch.
- Net new dependency on Redis for the request hot path. We accept this — Redis already gates session lookup.
author: marco.reyes

title: Auth Architecture Review (post-Safari incident)
snippet: Cross-subdomain auth review: cookie attributes, redirect chain, WebKit-specific behavior. Recommends strict cookie attrs + WebKit CI test.
full_text:
# Auth Architecture Review — May 2026
Authors: Marco Reyes, Priya Patel
Trigger: Safari login bug (May 4 weekend)

## Summary
Our auth flow worked by accident on Chrome/Firefox because they're more lenient on cross-site cookies than Safari/WebKit. The Safari outage was a foreseeable consequence of relying on default cookie attributes.

## Findings
1. Auth cookie did not set Secure or SameSite=None. Chrome/Firefox tolerated this; Safari 17 did not.
2. The redirect chain crosses two subdomains (mail.acme-co.com → app.acme-co.com) which triggers the strictest cross-site cookie rules.
3. Our test suite ran only against Chromium, so this regression was invisible in CI.

## Decisions
- D1: Set Secure + SameSite=None on all auth cookies. Already shipped (PR #188).
- D2: Add WebKit (Safari) target to Playwright CI. (Same PR.)
- D3: Document the cross-subdomain auth flow in /docs/architecture/auth.md (Marco, next sprint).

## Open questions
- Should we collapse mail.acme-co.com and app.acme-co.com onto a single subdomain to avoid this class of issue? Discussed; deferred — too much DNS surface to change for the current incident.
author: marco.reyes

# Cortex Web — Product PRD
Owner: Diane Park (PM)
Last updated: 2026-04-30

## What this product does
Cortex Web lets data teams import their event streams, run cohort/funnel analyses, and export results back to their warehouse or a flat file. Three jobs-to-be-done: import, analyze, export.

## Q2 product focus
Reliability at enterprise scale. Specifically:
- Export at scale (CSV v2, NDJSON support, column selection) — Northwind blocker.
- Auth that works across browsers without surprise outages (Safari incident May 4 catalyzed this).
- Backend reliability that isn't reset by every deploy (rate-limit refactor).

## Customer signals (top 3)
1. Northwind ($200k ARR) — gated on CSV v2 NDJSON support.
2. Beacon ($90k ARR) — flagged Safari login during their pilot.
3. Multiple SMB customers — frustrated with rate-limit hits during routine bulk operations.

title: CSV Export v2 — PRD
snippet: Customer ask synthesized from 14 tickets and 3 sales calls. NDJSON support is the #1 gap. Cursor pagination is the #2 gap.
full_text:
# CSV Export v2 — PRD
Owner: Diane Park
Last updated: 2026-05-01

## Customer evidence
- 14 tickets in Q1 about export size limits / timeouts.
- 3 sales conversations (Northwind, Beacon, Lattice) where export-at-scale was on the must-have list.
- 6 NPS responses calling out 'export is slow' or 'export breaks past 50k rows'.

## Top 3 gaps
1. **NDJSON output** — Northwind's data eng pipeline ingests NDJSON, not CSV. Hard requirement.
2. **Cursor pagination** — current export holds the full result in memory; OOMs past ~500k rows.
3. **Column selection** — customers don't want every column; payload size matters.

## Out of scope (this iteration)
- Scheduled / recurring exports.
- Webhook-triggered exports.
- Row-level templating / transforms.

## Engineering link
Design spec: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1xK9pP3vL_csv_export_v2_spec/edit

full_text:
# Postmortem — Safari login regression (Feb 2026)
Author: Marco Reyes
Incident date: 2026-02-14
Status: Closed (action items partially completed)

## What happened
For ~36 hours in mid-February, Safari users could not complete magic-link login. Root cause was a config change to the auth cookie domain that interacted poorly with WebKit's cross-site cookie rules.

## Action items (from Feb postmortem)
- [x] Roll back the cookie domain change.
- [x] Set explicit cookie attrs (Secure, SameSite, Domain).
- [ ] Add WebKit to Playwright CI matrix. **NOT DONE.** — *(this is why the May 4 regression slipped through)*
- [ ] Document cross-subdomain auth in /docs.

## Lessons relearned in May 2026
The Playwright-on-WebKit action item never landed because it was scoped as 'next sprint' and was deprioritized. The May incident is a direct consequence. Counter: adding WebKit CI is now in the same PR as the May fix (PR #188).

title: Telemetry Pipeline — Architecture (current)
snippet: Kafka → consumer group (3 instances) → Snowflake. Single consumer group; high-priority topics share with bulk topics.
full_text:
# Telemetry Pipeline — Current Architecture
Owner: Raj Kumar

## Topology
- Kafka cluster (3 brokers)
- Single consumer group (telemetry-cg) with 3 instances
- Snowflake sink via the kafka-connect-snowflake connector

## Known issues
- High-priority topics (auth-events, billing-events) share the consumer group with bulk topics (page-views), so a page-views backlog blocks billing-events processing.
- During peak load, lag hits 5-7 minutes.

## Proposed change
Split into two consumer groups: telemetry-cg-high (auth, billing) and telemetry-cg-bulk (everything else). Doubles infra cost but isolates the hot path.
author: raj.kumar
